pl-l3d34c9-d1e115.summary: Asks, since Christ had fear of penalty, whether this fear was worldly, servile, or initial.

pl-l3d34c9-d1e118.summary: Answers that none was in Christ: worldly fear is evil and abandoned at the first step, while servile and initial fear are not in perfect charity.
claims: Christ had none of the worldly, servile, or initial fears.

pl-l3d34c9-d1e121.summary: Identifies Christ's fear of penalty as natural or human fear, in all men, by which death is dreaded and penalty feared. It is called natural not as part of nature as first created, nor among natural goods, but because it came to all from nature corrupted by sin, as if natural; it is an effect of sin.
claims: Christ's fear of penalty was natural fear.
Natural fear came from nature corrupted by sin.

pl-l3d34c9.summary: Asks which fear Christ's fear of penalty was: worldly, servile, or initial. None, since worldly fear is evil and servile and initial fear are not in perfect charity. It can be called natural or human fear, present in all men, by which death is dreaded and penalty feared. It is called natural not because it belonged to nature as first created, but because through sin it came to all from corrupted nature as if natural; it is an effect of sin.
claims: Christ had none of the worldly, servile, or initial fears.
Christ's fear of penalty was natural or human fear.
Natural fear is an effect of sin, called natural because it pervades fallen nature.
